texts.preamble: Shri Anil Grover vs The Secretary on 31 August, 2022 In The Court Of Ms. Geetanjali, Additional District Judge05, South East District, Saket Courts, New Delhi Cs Dj No. 224/2017 Cnr No. Dlse010009642017 In the matter of : Shri Anil Grover Sole Proprietor of M/s. Groovy Foods (Division of Micro Devices Inc.) 306307, Bhandari House, 91, Nehru Place, New Delhi 110019 ....Plaintiff Vs. 1. The Secretary Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Government of India Maulana Azad Road, Rajpath Area, Central Secretariat, New Delhi 110001 ..... Defendant No. 1 2. Foods Safety and Standards Authority of India (Fssai) Through the Chairperson Fda Bhawan, Kotla Road, New Delhi 110002 ..... Defendant No. 2
texts.facts: SUIT FOR RECOVERY OF Rs.43,29,026/ JUDGMENT 1. Vide this Judgment, I intend to dispose off the suit for recovery of Rs. 43,29,026/ inclusive of interest against the defendants. 2. The factual matrix of the case is that the Plaintiff is the sole proprietor of M/s. Groovy Foods, a proprietorship concern and is engaged in the business of cocoa powder and industrial chocolates. In pursuit of its business, it imported 'cocoa powder from the producer/seller "Altinmarka" in Turkey vide two consignments after payment in advance in the year 2013 in respect whereof NOC was also obtained from defendant no. 2 Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (in short "FSSAI") prior to clearance from Customs as per procedure. On each occasion the samples were withdrawn by FSSAI and NOC was issued after testing only. The plaintiff again imported "cocoa powder" from Shri Anil Grover vs The Secretary on 31 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110959933/ 1 Altinmarka after making the advance payment for the goods vide invoice no. 9199465 dated 31.12.2013 for an amount of Rs.12,15,879/ and paid freight charges of Rs.96,430/ to freight forwarder and the goods arrived in India on 24.01.2014. The bill of entry no. 4478803 dated 28.01.2014 was filed which was okayed by Customs and duty amount of Rs.6,64,349/ was paid 30.01.2014. As per requirement of the Customs, the plaintiff applied for NOC to FSSAI for these goods after paying sampling charges of Rs.6742/ on 07.02.2014. However surprisingly they received an email from FSSAI on 08.02.2014 with remarks against 'Visual inspection details: Any Rectifiable Discrepancy Observed" "Yes" but no reason or alleged discrepancy was set out therein nor any details of sample withdrawn or result of sample analysis disclosed. Vide letter dated 10.02.2014, the plaintiff was informed CS DJ No. 224/2017 page no. 2 of 16 that NOC cannot be accepted for the reason that the ingredient list was not mentioned on the label as per alleged mandatory labeling requirements under FSSAI regulations. The plaintiff immediately submitted a detailed representation dated 11.02.2014 to Mr. S. Dave, Advisor of FSSAI giving details of earlier imports which were cleared with NOC from FSSAI and referring to the FSSAI regulations and Codex 105 standards and submitted copies of all previous bill of entries alongwith previous NOC issued by FSSAI for the same product. He finally met Mr. Dave on 25.02.2014 and explained and clarified in detail that the product as imported carried the labeling as per FSSAI regulation and Codex 105 standard only and he was assured that he would receive a response within 48 hours. However there was no response from FSSAI despite sending several emails to them. Due to this enormous delay on the part of FSSAI and its failure to correctly apply its own regulations inspite of consistent follow up by the plaintiff led to heavy financial burden and the plaintiff was left with no option but to re export the shipment since he could not get the clearance. The permission to reexport was granted on 24.10.2014 subject to fine and penalty of Rs.1,00,000/ and Rs.50,000/. Apart from that the plaintiff firm also paid the detention charges of Rs.3,72,583/ and Rs.4,53,409/ on 29.10.2014 to Oriental Overseas Container Line plus storage charges of Rs.3,88,700/ to CONCOR and customs clearance charges of Rs.1,25,372/ on 30.10.2014 plus Rs.1,06,032/ paid to the freight forwarder for re export on 05.12.2014. However the penalty amount was refunded by the defendant on 06.08.2015 in view of the order passed by the Commissioner of Appeals. Thereafter plaintiff got issued legal notice dated 08.11.2016 to the defendant thereby demanding the said charges but defendants neither CS DJ No. 224/2017 page no. 3 of 16 replied the said notice nor made any payment which compelled the plaintiff to knock at the doors of the Court for payment of said amount through the present suit. 3. Summons sent to defendant no. 1 received back served on 14.02.2017 however none appeared on their behalf nor the written statement was filed within the stipulated period and hence their right to file the written statement was closed and they were proceeded exparte vide order dated 16.03.2017. 3.1 Defendant no. 2 filed detailed written statement taking preliminary objections to the effect that the plaintiff has not complied with the provisions of Food and Safety Act, 2006 and its rules and regulations; that vide letter dated 10.02.2014 it was clarified that product of the plaintiff cannot be assessed without knowing the ingredients which ought to have been mentioned as per the mandatory labeling requirements contained in FSS Regulations, 2011; that the product of the plaintiff was non conforming to section 23 of FSS Act and Regulations 2.2.2.2 and 2.6.1 of the FSS (Packaging and Labeling Regulations), 2011 and the plaintiff had deliberately not uploaded the copy Shri Anil Grover vs The Secretary on 31 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110959933/ 2 of the label in Food Import Clearance System (FICS); that the existing label of the product of the plaintiff is in violation of the said regulations. 3.2 In reply on merits, defendant no. 2 has denied all the material contents of the suit and prayed for its dismissal. 3.3 The plaintiff has filed replication to the written statement of defendant no. 2 thereby reaffirming and reiterating the contents of plaint and denying the contents of written statement. 4. From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed vide CS DJ No. 224/2017 page no. 4 of 16 order dated 07.07.2017: 1. OPD 4. Relief. Thereafter, matter was fixed for plaintiff's evidence. 5. In order to prove its case, the plaintiff examined four more witnesses apart from him. He examined himself as PW1 and reiterated the facts of plaint in his affidavit Ex.PW1/A. He has relied upon the documents i.e. Ex. PW1/1 to Ex. PW1/44. He was extensively crossexamined by ld. Counsel for the defendant no. 2. 5.1 PW2 Shri Amarnath, Senior Manager, Dena Bank was summoned to prove payment made towards various charges by the plaintiff which are exhibited as Ex. PW2/1 (colly.) to Ex. PW2/6. 5.2 PW3 Shri Naveen Meena, Clerk, Bank of India was summoned to prove payment made towards Customs duty by the plaintiff which are exhibited as Ex.PW3/1 to Ex. PW3/3. 5.3 PW4 Shri Yash Jain, Service Delivery Manager, Indusind Bank was summoned to prove the statement of account and exhibited the same as Ex. PW4/1 (colly.) to Ex. PW4/3. 5.4 PW5 Shri Vikas Kumar, Deputy Manager, ICICI Bank was CS DJ No. 224/2017 page no. 5 of 16 Shri Anil Grover vs The Secretary on 31 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110959933/ 3 summoned to prove the transaction details which are exhibited as Ex.PW5/1 to Ex. PW5/6. Thereafter, matter was fixed for defendant's evidence. They examined their Deputy Director Shri Anil Mehta as DW1. He has tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. DW1/A thereby reiterating the defence taken in the written statement. He has relied on the documents i.e. Ex. DW1/1 (colly.). He was extensively cross examined by the counsel for the plaintiff. She was extensively cross examined by the counsel for the plaintiff. The onus to prove issue no. 1 and 2 was placed upon the plaintiff and that of issue no. 3 was upon the defendant. 9. The plaintiff has filed present suit for the recovery of Rs.43,29,026/.
texts.arguments: 10. Per contra PW1 has deposed that "the plaintiff had with utmost caution and diligence gone through all the procedural requirements regarding labelling of his import which related to "wholesale packages" and in respect whereof, sub section 4 of Article 2.6.1 provides as following: Shri Anil Grover vs The Secretary on 31 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110959933/ 5 "In case of wholesale packages the particulars regarding list of ingredients, date of manufacture/packing, best before, expiry date, labelling of irradiated food and, vegetarian logo/non vegetarian logo, may not be specified" That the plaintiff had imported a wholesale package of Cocoa powder and hence the above mentioned particulars did not need to be mentioned. 11. The said stand of plaintiff is countered by the defendants vide para no. 4 of preliminary submissions wherein it is submitted that the guidelines that were issued by FSSAI bearing number 117/FSSAI/T/2010 dated 23.03.2012 clearly mentioned in para1: CS DJ No. 224/2017 page no. 9 of 16 " It states that "no person shall manufacture, distribute, sell or expose for sale of dispatch or deliver to any agent or broker for the purpose of sale, any packaged food products which are not market and labelled in the manner as may be specified by regulations:" The Hon'ble Bombay High Court in "Vital Nutraceuticals Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Union of India & Anr., dated 30.06.2014" has held that ".....The Food Authority which is obliged to do something by way of framing regulations, cannot be allowed to do the same by issuing advisories. The said judgment has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court vide judgment dated 19.08.2015 passed in "Food Safety and Standards Authority of India Vs. Vital Nutraceuticals Pvt. Ltd. & Ors."
